root_cause.text: The `nft_meta_bridge_get_eval()` function only copies 6 bytes (`ETH_ALEN`) of the hardware address into a destination register span that is rounded up to 8 bytes (two 32-bit registers), leaving the remaining 2 bytes uninitialized and leaking stale stack data to userspace.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows the addition of `dest[1] = 0;` before `memcpy(dest, br_dev->dev_addr, ETH_ALEN);` to zero out the second register, and the commit message states that "NFT_META_BRI_IIFHWADDR declares its destination register with len = ETH_ALEN (6 bytes), which the register-init tracking rounds up to two 32-bit registers (8 bytes)", resulting in "leaving the upper 2 bytes of the second register as uninitialised nft_do_chain() stack."

Author: Fernando Fernandez Mancera <fmancera@suse.de>

    netfilter: nft_meta_bridge: introduce NFT_META_BRI_IIFHWADDR support
    
    Expose the input bridge interface ethernet address so it can be used to

    Tested with nft command line tool.
    
    table bridge nat {
            chain PREROUTING {
                    type filt
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the NFT_META_BRI_IIFHWADDR support. In nft_meta_bridge_get_eval(), it copies ETH_ALEN (6 bytes) to the destination register using memcpy(dest, br_dev->dev_addr, ETH_ALEN). In nft_meta_bridge_get_init(), the length is set to ETH_ALEN. Because register sizes are rounded up to 4-byte boundaries (making a 6-byte value occupy 8 bytes of register space), the remaining 2 bytes of the register are left uninitialized, leaking stale stack data.
